polityNote: Portuguese Angola (districts) from the creation of the Cunene district (1970-07-10) to independence, then the People's Republic / Republic of Angola (Cabinda included throughout). Atoms are the 558 communes of geoBoundaries AGO ADM3 (INE Angola, 2014 census; CC BY 3.0). Each commune is assigned to its 2014 municipality and province by name from the census list (all 558 names match; the province of every commune also agrees with the geoBoundaries AGO ADM1 2021 province it lies in, 551 of 558 at ≥99% of their area). Earlier provinces are unions of whole municipalities moved by named laws (Bengo 1980, Lei 29/11 of 2011) or splits of a province by whole municipalities (Lunda 1978). Independent check (①): the 2014 province unions agree with the published province areas (geohive/INE as tabulated in en.wikipedia Angola rev. 1377670946) within 3.0% for every unchanged province (e.g. Huambo 33,261 vs 33,296 km², Huíla 78,969 vs 78,897, Cuanza Sul 55,479 vs 55,554, Cabinda 7,021 vs 7,270).

unresolved.what: Districts of Portuguese West Africa / Angola before the Cunene district (1900 → 1970-07-10)
unresolved.why: The district map was redrawn repeatedly (1901 Huíla; 1911 Huambo; 1914/1917 Cuanza; 1917 Moxico; 1919 Cabinda; 1921 Malanje; 1922 Bié and Zaire; 1930 reduction to eight districts; 1934 five provinces; decree 40 225 of 1955-06-05 thirteen districts; DLM 6 and 51 of 1961 Uíge/Zaire and Cuando Cubango). The 1960 areas of the thirteen districts (statoids, Britannica World Atlas 1964) differ from the unions of their successor provinces' 2014 communes by far more than measurement (Moçâmedes 34,340 km² vs 58,131; Huíla 188,830 vs Huíla+Cunene 156,475; Malanje 114,060 vs 88,475; Cuanza Sul 44,850 vs 55,479; Cuanza Norte 31,210 vs 24,228), so concelhos/circunscrições moved between districts at dates no consulted source names.
